Writing a sheet

A sheet is a list of statements, one per line or separated by semicolons. Dome solves the sheet as a system: the order of the lines does not matter, and an unknown may sit on either side of an equation. This page follows the first example, Help › Examples › First sheet: equations and units.

Equations and units

p   = 2 [bar]
V_1 = 40 [L]
T_1 = 27 [C]
W   = 6 [kJ]
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)
T_2 / T_1 = V_2 / V_1
  • Equations. a = b in any arrangement. Dome matches equations to unknowns, evaluates the explicit ones directly and solves the rest by iteration. Equations that repeat each other, contradict each other or leave a variable undetermined are reported on their line.
  • Units. A unit follows a number in square brackets. Everything after a slash is in the denominator, so [kJ/kg·K] is kJ/(kg·K); *, ^ and parentheses also work. Values are converted to SI on entry, so bar, kPa, L and kJ can be mixed. A number without a unit where one is needed is an error.
  • Unit conversion. Dividing by a unit gives a plain number in that unit: p_kPa = p / (1 [kPa]).
  • Values shown. SI or English in the header sets the units results are shown in.

Temperatures and temperature changes

[C], [K], [F] or [R] alone is a temperature. Dome holds temperatures in kelvin, so a ratio such as T_2 / T_1 is a ratio of absolute temperatures. A change in temperature is written in [K] or [R]: T_1 + 20 [K] with T_1 = 27 [C] is 47 °C. A negative value in [K] or [R], such as dT = -10 [K], is a change.

Comments and sections

Text after % is a comment. %% at the start of a line begins a section in published reports; the first section's text is the report's default title.

%% Boundary work
% Equations can be written in any order.
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)    % work done by the gas

Checks and starting values

  • check compares two expressions after the sheet is solved: check V_2 > V_1. The comparisons are ==, <=, >=, < and >. The result appears at the right of the line and under the Checks tab.
  • Two answers. When two values of a variable satisfy an equation, as for x^2 - 5*x + 6 = 0, a check line on that variable chooses between them: with check x > 2.5, Dome uses 3. Without one, Dome keeps the value its iteration found and names it on the line. Dome reports a second value when its search of one equation finds one: equations solved together are not searched, and the search can miss a value close to the one used, so a line with no warning may still have a second answer.
  • guess sets the starting value of a variable found by iteration: guess T_2 = 400 [K]. Dome takes a starting value from the units of each unknown, so a sheet rarely needs one. A guess line is for a solve that Dome reports could not start, or found no solution from its starting values.

Problems

A line Dome cannot use is underlined in the sheet, and the Problems tab lists it with its line number and the reason. Holding the pointer over the underline shows the reason in the sheet. Below, the line Q = W + dU was added to the first example; nothing else in the sheet determines dU, so the sheet has fewer equations than unknowns.

The Math view

The Math view shows the sheet typeset as equations, with the value of each line. It is available in two places: the Code and Math buttons in the sheet's header switch the sheet pane, and the pane menu of any other pane can show Math beside the sheet, as above.

Keys and completion

With the cursor in the sheet, ⌘Enter (CtrlEnter on Windows and Linux) solves it; in the sweep editor the same keys run the sweep. With Auto-solve checked in the header, the sheet is solved after each edit. CtrlSpace completes a name, unit or fluid; on macOS, where CtrlSpace often switches the input source, Option` does the same.

Language reference

Help › Reference opens this reference in a pane beside the current panes. The text below is taken from that pane when this manual is built, so the two always match. Keys are listed as on macOS; on Windows and Linux, Ctrl takes the place of ⌘.

Statements

a = b + cEquation. Unknowns may appear on either side; the sheet is solved as a system.
x = 3; y = 4One statement per line, or separated by semicolons.
% textComment. %% at the start of a line begins a section in published reports.
fluid waterFluid for the states that follow: water, r134a, r22, ammonia, propane, air.
state 1 : p = …, T = …State from two independent properties among p, T, v, u, h, s, x. Defines p_1, T_1, v_1, u_1, h_1, s_1, x_1.
state 2 (r134a) : …State of a fluid other than the current one.
check a == bComparison evaluated after solving; also <=, >=, <, >.
guess T_2 = 400 [K]Starting value for a variable found by iteration. Needed only when Dome reports that a solve could not start or found no solution from its starting values.
plot Ts : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3Property diagram: Ts, pv, ph or hs.

Units

80 [bar]A unit follows a number in brackets. Values are converted to SI internally.
480 [C]A temperature unit alone (C, K, F, R) is a temperature. A change in temperature is written in K or R: T_1 + 10 [K].
T_2 - T_1A difference of two temperatures is a change, shown in K (°R in English units). A temperature plus or minus a change is a temperature.
[kJ/kg·K]Everything after a slash is in the denominator. Also *, ^ and parentheses.
unitskg g lb m cm mm ft in s min h K C F R N kN lbf Pa kPa MPa bar atm psi J kJ MJ Btu kWh W kW MW hp L gal

Functions

h(water, p = p_2, s = s_1)Property of a fluid at a state given by two named properties. Also p, T, v, u, s, x, cp, cv, rho.
Tsat(water, p = 1 [bar])Saturation temperature; psat(water, T = …) is the saturation pressure.
ln exp sqrt absAlso log10, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, min, max.

Plot paths

-p- -s- -T- -v- -h-Process at constant pressure, entropy, temperature, specific volume or enthalpy. Drawn dashed when that property differs between the two states.
--Straight line.

Sweep

sweep T_3 = 320:20:600 [C]     % start:step:stop, or a list: 5, 7, 9
record eta, x_4
plot eta, x_4 vs T_3

The swept variable must be an input: a line name = number [unit], or a number written in a state line (x = 0 in state 3 makes x_3 an input).

Properties

CoolProp 7.2.1dev (Helmholtz equations of state; air as an ideal gas with variable specific heats). Enthalpy, internal energy and entropy are shifted to the reference states of the Moran and Shapiro tables. Differences between states, and the cycle results built from them, agree closely with the tables; a single value can differ from the printed table by about 1 kJ/kg, and by up to about 5 kJ/kg in parts of the superheated tables. Answers graded in ENES232 use the printed tables.

Keys

⌘EnterSolve, with the cursor in the sheet; in the sweep editor, run the sweep
⌘S, ⌘⇧SSave, save as
⌘O, ⌘NOpen, new
⌘Z, ⌘⇧ZUndo, redo
Ctrl+Space, ⌥`Complete a name, unit or fluid, in the sheet or the sweep editor
